description: We are a team from MFLab, a Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) research laboratory at the Federal University of Uberlândia, Brazil. Our background includes scientific computing, software development, numerical simulations, and data analysis. We are passionate about science, technology, and space exploration, and we welcome creative, curious people with skills in programming, design, astronomy, or related fields to join us!
summary:
SPHEREx, NASA's all-sky infrared survey, images the entire sky every six months in 102 wavelength bands. Asteroids, comets, nearby stars and brown dwarfs reveal themselves by shifting position between exposures, but the volume of data is too large for a few specialists to inspect.
SkyBrew bridges citizen science and professional astronomy through a progressive dual-layer architecture. For curious beginners, SkyBrew abstracts complex physics into guided workflows. Users can hunt for asteroids, brown dwarfs, or variable stars using intent-based automated band stacking and time-lapse flipbooks, while learning how to identify celestial objects in images through interactive quizzes. In Professional mode, astronomers choose a field by typing coordinates or by navigating an interactive sky map, pick the infrared detectors, compare the images with the Gaia DR3 catalog, and export a candidate report with its position and time. Every search has its own link, so it can be shared or embedded in other websites. To demonstrate the tool, SkyBrew includes instant one-click benchmarks for NASA-suggested test targets (WISE 0855, Barnard's Star, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis).
details:
What it does & how it works

SkyBrew helps people spot changes in the sky by playing real SPHEREx images of the same region in sequence. It retrieves Level-2 images and observation metadata from NASA/IPAC IRSA, checks which exposures can be compared, and aligns them by sky coordinates before playback.

  • Citizen Science Mode: Volunteers select a target category and receive a randomly sampled sky field. SkyBrew automatically configures the appropriate detector bands for that goal and retrieves images with overlapping coverage to build a time-lapse blink sequence. Users can mark candidate objects directly on the blinking viewer, supported by interactive tutorials and a quiz that introduce moving objects, variable brightness, known sources, and detector artifacts. 
  • Professional Mode: Users can enter right ascension and declination, choose a field size and select one or more infrared detectors (D1–D6). An Aladin Lite sky map supports navigation. The viewer provides blink sequences, combinations of overlapping detector images, temporal stacking and subtraction, quick-look spectral graphs, catalog markers, quality flags and an adjustable WISE reference image. Users can also browse the 102 nominal channels of a separate SPHEREx all-sky visual map. Search coordinates, field size and detector selection can be shared in a URL or opened in an iframe.

Benefits

  • Goal-Oriented Infrared Presets: Abstracts complex 102-band near-infrared physics into goal-oriented presets (Asteroids, Brown Dwarfs, Variable Stars), enabling non-experts to analyze multi-spectral data without manual channel management.
  • Training with real examples: Tutorials and a quiz teach volunteers what to examine and how to check artifacts and quality flags before reporting a candidate.
  • Stable blink sequences: SkyBrew groups exposures by shared coverage and places their FITS images on a common sky-coordinate grid, making changes easier to see across frames.
  • Spectral exploration: Professionals can browse 102 nominal channels in the time-combined SPHEREx DR1 sky map. From loaded Level-2 exposures, they can also plot a quick-look spectrum at a selected position or compare bright-pixel signal across wavelengths in the whole field. 
  • Temporal comparisons: Professionals can stack selected exposures from one detector using inverse-variance weights or subtract two aligned images. When both images provide suitable ePSF models, subtraction can optionally match their central point-spread functions. 
  • WISE reference imagery: An adjustable AllWISE infrared image can be overlaid on the professional sky map and image viewer to compare SPHEREx with an earlier survey. It is aligned by sky coordinates but was observed at different times and wavelengths.
  • Reference markers: Gaia DR3, AllWISE and 2MASS catalog positions, along with predicted positions of known Solar System objects from IMCCE SkyBoT, can be displayed over the images. This eliminates user confusion, prevents redundant tagging of established targets, and directs volunteer screening toward genuine candidate discoveries.
  • Image-quality inspection: Users can highlight pixels flagged for caution or lacking usable data and inspect the original flags for individual detector images.
  • Interactive Multi-Candidate Tagging: Users mark candidate objects directly on the time-lapse frames. Each candidate receives its own persistent identifier, so several targets in the same field can be followed across the sequence without their marks being mixed up and their recorded information can be also kept separate. 
  • Sub-Pixel Alignment: A magnified alignment tool with sub-pixel adjustment controls lets users place the center marker precisely on faint sources before recording.
  • Quick Trials: Bundled SPHEREx image sets for Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae and R Draconis open without waiting for a new IRSA image request. The WISE 0855 marker shows a predicted position; its identification in individual SPHEREx exposures has not been verified.
  • Shareable fields: URLs preserve coordinates, field size and detector selection for bookmarking and embedding.

Intended Impact:
By empowering both researchers and the public, Skybrew fosters collaborative innovation, accelerates the pace of scientific discovery in the era of big data, and democratizes space science. 

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software: 

  • Client & Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, CDS Aladin Lite v3 Engine. 
  • Serverless Backend & API: TypeScript Vercel Functions (/api/search, /api/frame, /api/catalog/stars, /api/catalog/solar) Custom TypeScript FITS reader verified against independent Python extractions.
